summary: GxEPD2 thread: read the GxEPD2 master (=1.6.9, tagged 2026-04-19) sources raw from GitHub, the local Arduino-ESP32 3.3.8 core sources, the firmware, and the Seeed ePaper Driver Board schematic. Headline results: (a) class GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 exists (added 1.5.0 as GxEPD2_750_YT7, renamed 1.5.4), and the firmware's template instantiation is a true single-page 48,000-byte full-frame buffer. (b) The white-stripe hypothesis is CONFIRMED by source, but it is always exactly 4 columns, in a fixed pattern: refreshing a square on files a/c/e/g whitens the 4 leftmost columns of the b/d/f/h neighbour; refreshing b/d/f/h whitens the 4 rightmost columns of a/c/e/g. 1.e4 already leaves stripes on f2 and f4. drawSquare also erases the board border on edge squares. (c) For this panel GxEPD2 sets usePartialUpdateWindow=false, so EVERY 'partial' refresh is a whole-screen differential refresh costing ~435 ms regardless of window size; the firmware's 3 sequential refreshes per move cost ~1.35 s (+0.45 s for the selection tap) versus ~0.45-0.65 s for one refresh from a persistent full buffer (display(true) / displayWindow / or epd2.writeImagePart xN + epd2.refresh(true)). No partial-window size limit exists. (d) The firmware never calls powerOff()/hibernate() after partial refreshes, so the panel's HV booster stays on for the whole time the player thinks; and it counts moves, not refreshes, so ~80 partial refreshes happen between 'full' refreshes while Good Display recommends a full refresh every 5; GxEPD2's 'full' is in fact the 1.17 s single-flash fast-full (compile-time const). (e) init(115200,true,2,false): the 2 ms reset is a Waveshare-specific workaround; the Seeed schematic shows RST wired straight to the FPC, so the default 10 ms is the right value. BUSY stuck = 10 s timeout per wait with 'Busy Timeout!' on Serial, never a hang. (f) SPI.begin(sck,miso,mosi,ss) before display.init() is the correct and author-documented remap method on ESP32 (GxEPD2's own begin() becomes a no-op: 'if (_spi) return true;'); selectSPI does not set pins. Pass MISO=-1 so GPIO8 is not double-claimed by SPI and the buzzer (on core 3.3.8 it happens to survive). (g) 4-grey is not in GxEPD2; GxEPD2_4G 1.0.8+ supports the panel but grey partial updates 'look bad', so stay 1-bit. (h) For pieces use two 1-bit bitmaps per piece (dilated white mask + black ink) rasterised offline from SVG; GPL-3.0-compatible sets per lichess COPYING.md: cburnett/mono/merida (GPLv2+), mpchess (GPLv3+), fantasy/spatial/celtic (MIT), chessnut (Apache-2.0), rhosgfx (CC0), CC BY 4.0 sets; avoid all CC BY-NC-SA and 'freeware' sets. Transparency note: I created no files, but the WebFetch tool itself auto-saved the Seeed schematic PDF under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-fabriziodrago-Downloads-collecticraft-studio/a3ff4289-01a0-4361-8319-c3a9a6600518/tool-results/webfetch-1790014284505-d9s2fc.pdf. Nothing was compiled or installed.

findings.claim: Class GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 exists in every release >= 1.5.4 (so in ^1.6.2). Support for the panel was added in 1.5.0 as GxEPD2_750_YT7 and renamed in 1.5.4. Latest release is 1.6.9 (2026-04-19); PlatformIO '^1.6.2' will resolve to 1.6.9. Constants are identical at tags 1.6.2 and 1.6.9: WIDTH=800, HEIGHT=480, hasPartialUpdate=true, hasFastPartialUpdate=true, usePartialUpdateWindow=false, useFastFullUpdate=true, useFastPartialUpdateFromOTP=true, power_on_time=140, power_off_time=42, full_refresh_time=1200, partial_refresh_time=450 (ms). Constructor: GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7(int16_t cs, int16_t dc, int16_t rst, int16_t busy); busy level LOW, busy timeout 10 s, default SPI 4 MHz mode 0.
findings.evidence: Header lines 23-38: 'static const uint16_t WIDTH = 800; ... HEIGHT = 480; ... hasPartialUpdate = true; usePartialUpdateWindow = false; // set false for better image; hasFastPartialUpdate = true; useFastFullUpdate = true; // set false for extended (low) temperature range; useFastPartialUpdateFromOTP = true; // set this false for earlier batches, such as the panel I have (1580258us); power_on_time = 140; // ms, e.g. 129018us; power_off_time = 42; full_refresh_time = 1200; // ms, e.g. 1171000us; partial_refresh_time = 450; // ms, e.g. 435000us'. cpp line 17: 'GxEPD2_EPD(cs, dc, rst, busy, LOW, 10000000, WIDTH, HEIGHT, panel, ...)'. GxEPD2_EPD.cpp line 24: '_spi_settings(4000000, MSBFIRST, SPI_MODE0)'. README: 'Version 1.5.0 - added support for GDEY075T7 7.5" b/w 800x480'; 'Version 1.5.4 - renamed driver class GxEPD2_750_YT7 to GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 - the actual GDEY075T7 panels have fast full refresh capability'; 'Version 1.5.9 - added Power Save command (PWS) to GDEY075T7 init (issue with dithered bitmaps)'; 'Version 1.6.6 - added method writeImageToPrevious to class GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 and nextPageToPrevious to GxEPD2_BW'. library.properties: version=1.6.9; GitHub tags API lists 1.6.9 as newest, commit dated 2026-04-19. LICENSE = GPL v3.
findings.recommended_action: Keep 'zinggjm/GxEPD2 @ ^1.6.2' or pin '@ 1.6.9' for reproducible MakerWorld builds (1.6.6+ is needed for nextPageToPrevious if hibernate() is used). Firmware licence must be GPL-3.0(-or-later) because GxEPD2 is GPL-3.0.

findings.claim: GxEPD2_BW<GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7, GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7::HEIGHT> is a full-frame buffer: 48,000 bytes, exactly one page, held inside the global display object (.bss, internal SRAM).
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_BW.h line 815: 'uint8_t _buffer[(GxEPD2_Type::WIDTH / 8) * page_height];' = 100*480 = 48000. Lines 247-248: '_page_height = page_height; _pages = (HEIGHT / _page_height) + ((HEIGHT % _page_height) > 0);' = 1. nextPage() line 431 takes the 'if (1 == _pages)' branch. README: 'full screen buffer is selected by setting template parameter page_height to display height - drawing to full screen buffer can either be done using Adafruit_GFX methods without picture loop ... and then calling method display()'.
findings.recommended_action: Exploit it: keep the buffer persistent between moves (never call firstPage()/fillScreen for incremental updates) and push with display(true)/displayWindow(). See GX-06.

findings.claim: init(115200, true, 2, false) = (serial_diag_bitrate, initial, reset_duration_ms, pulldown_rst_mode). 115200>0 calls Serial.begin() and enables timing diagnostics ('_PowerOn : us', '_Update_Part : us'). initial=true forces a full-buffer clear on first write and a full refresh on first refresh. reset_duration=2 is a workaround ONLY for Waveshare boards with the 'clever' power-cutting reset circuit; the Seeed ePaper Driver Board wires RST straight from XIAO D0 to the FPC (no transistor/RC), so the library default 10 ms is the appropriate value. pulldown_rst_mode=false = push-pull RST (true is for avoiding 5 V back-feed).
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_BW.h lines 317-323: 'initial false for re-init after processor deep sleep wake up, if display power supply was kept ... NOTE: garbage will result on fast partial update displays, if initial full update is omitted after power loss ... reset_duration = 10 is default; a value of 2 may help with "clever" reset circuit of newer boards from Waveshare ... pulldown_rst_mode true for alternate RST handling to avoid feeding 5V through RST pin'. GxEPD2_EPD.cpp _reset(): 'digitalWrite(_rst, HIGH); ... delay(10); digitalWrite(_rst, LOW); delay(_reset_duration); digitalWrite(_rst, HIGH); delay(_reset_duration > 10 ? _reset_duration : 10);'. GxEPD2_Example.ino lines 201-202: 'display.init(115200); // default 10ms reset pulse, e.g. for bare panels with DESPI-C02' vs '// USE THIS for Waveshare boards with "clever" reset circuit, 2ms reset pulse'. Seeed schematic 'ePAPER' Rev 1.0 (2024-12-09): net A0_D0_RST goes directly from the XIAO socket to CN_DISPLAY; BUSY/DC/CS/SCK/MOSI likewise direct, no pull-ups, no series parts.
findings.recommended_action: Change to display.init(115200, true, 10, false) (or plain display.init(115200)). 2 ms will most likely also work (UC8179 minimum reset width not verified), but there is no reason to use the Waveshare workaround. Keep diag bitrate >0 during bring-up: the printed _Update_Part/_Update_Full microseconds are the cheapest way to measure the real panel timings; set 0 for release.

findings.claim: If BUSY never changes (panel/FPC not connected) GxEPD2 does NOT hang: each wait times out after 10 s, prints 'Busy Timeout!' and continues. With BUSY stuck LOW the phase-1 boot blocks ~30 s (PowerOn + Update_Full + PowerOff) and every later partial ~10-20 s; with BUSY floating HIGH all waits return in ~1 ms and the code 'succeeds' instantly with nothing displayed. The Seeed board has no pull resistor on BUSY, so with the FPC unplugged GPIO3 floats and either behaviour can occur.
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_EPD.cpp _waitWhileBusy lines 139-175: 'if (digitalRead(_busy) != _busy_level) break; ... if (micros() - start > _busy_timeout) { Serial.println("Busy Timeout!"); break; } ... yield(); // avoid wdt'. _busy_level=LOW and _busy_timeout=10000000 from the GDEY075T7 constructor (cpp line 17). Waits occur in _PowerOn, _PowerOff, _Update_Full, _Update_Part. Schematic: BUSY net has no pull-up/down.
findings.recommended_action: Add a bring-up self-test: time the first full refresh; if it is < ~300 ms or > ~5 s, print/beep 'display not detected - check FPC orientation' (an upside-down FPC is the classic failure with this panel per the Arduino forum thread 1355813). A plausible _Update_Full is ~1.1-1.3 s.

findings.claim: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED (with a correction: always exactly 4 columns, never 5-7). drawSquare() corrupts the horizontally adjacent square in the same rank. Files a,c,e,g (x = 0,120,240,360, x%8==0): window becomes [x, x+64) so columns x+60..x+63 = the 4 LEFTMOST columns of the b/d/f/h neighbour are overwritten with white (absolute columns 60-63, 180-183, 300-303, 420-423). Files b,d,f,h (x = 60,180,300,420, x%8==4): window becomes [x-4, x+60) so the 4 RIGHTMOST columns of the a/c/e/g neighbour are whitened (56-59, 176-179, 296-299, 416-419). Damage never crosses pair boundaries (120 px = 15 bytes) and never extends vertically (rotation 0). Because same-rank neighbours always have the opposite colour, refreshing any LIGHT square leaves a 4x60 px white stripe in the hatched DARK neighbour (hatch dots sit at column offsets 0,2,...,58 so both edge strips contain dots). Example: 1.e4 -> e2 and e4 are light -> stripes on f2 and f4 at x=300..303. Related second artefact: paintSquare()'s fillRect(x,y,60,60,WHITE) also erases the board border drawn only in drawFull() (x=0, x=479, y=0, y=479) on every refreshed edge square. The status strip (x=480,w=320) is byte-aligned and harmless.
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_BW.h setPartialWindow lines 415-418: '// make _pw_x, _pw_w multiple of 8 / _pw_w += _pw_x % 8; if (_pw_w % 8 > 0) _pw_w += 8 - _pw_w % 8; _pw_x -= _pw_x % 8;'. firstPage lines 422-427: 'fillScreen(GxEPD_WHITE);' (whole buffer 0xFF). drawPixel lines 292-306 clips to the widened window and indexes 'x / 8 + y * (_pw_w / 8)', so the extra columns are addressable but the firmware never paints them. nextPage lines 433-436 (1 page, partial): 'epd2.writeImage(_buffer, _pw_x, _pw_y, _pw_w, _pw_h); epd2.refresh(_pw_x, _pw_y, _pw_w, _pw_h);' -> the full widened 64x60 block (8 bytes/row) goes to controller RAM 0x13; driver _writeImage repeats the alignment ('x -= x % 8; w = wb * 8'). Firmware board_ui.cpp lines 80-85: 'setPartialWindow(x, y, SQ, SQ); firstPage(); do { paintSquare(b, file, rank, highlight); } while (nextPage());' paints one square only. Line 26 fillRect covers the border pixels; border drawn only at line 69 in drawFull. Per-file windows computed numerically: a [0,64), b [56,120), c [120,184), d [176,240), e [240,304), f [296,360), g [360,424), h [416,480). Hatch density computed = 12.5%.
findings.recommended_action: Preferred: drop setPartialWindow()/firstPage() for incremental updates and keep a persistent full-frame buffer (GX-06); the widened bytes then carry the neighbour's real pixels and both artefacts vanish (redraw the border inside paintSquare or after it). Minimal patch if the page loop is kept: inside the do-loop also paint the pair neighbour (file ^ 1) and the border. Alternative layout fix: 56 px squares (7 bytes) -> 448 px board, byte-aligned everywhere, and 32 px left over for a-h/1-8 coordinates.

verification.corrected_claim: Claim stands as written: drawSquare() whitens exactly 4 columns of the same-rank pair neighbour (a<->b, c<->d, e<->f, g<->h): cols x+60..x+63 when refreshing a/c/e/g, cols x-4..x-1 when refreshing b/d/f/h. Visible as a 4x60 white stripe whenever the refreshed square is light (neighbour hatched), plus 4 px of top/bottom border on rank-1/8 neighbours; paintSquare's fillRect additionally erases the board border on every refreshed edge square. Fixes are valid: persistent full-frame buffer (GX-06), or paint neighbour (file ^ 1) + border inside the page loop, or 56 px squares with BOARD_X a multiple of 8.
verification.reasoning: Re-fetched GxEPD2_BW.h (master = 1.6.9, which '^1.6.2' in platformio.ini resolves to) and re-read board_ui.cpp myself. setPartialWindow(): '_pw_w += _pw_x % 8; if (_pw_w % 8 > 0) _pw_w += 8 - _pw_w % 8; _pw_x -= _pw_x % 8;'. Recomputed for SQ=60, BOARD_X=0, rotation 0: x%8==0 files (a,c,e,g) -> w 60->64, window [x,x+64); x%8==4 files (b,d,f,h) -> w 60+4=64, x-=4, window [x-4,x+60). Exactly 4 foreign columns every time, always inside the same 120 px file pair; no y alignment is applied so no vertical spill. firstPage() = fillScreen(GxEPD_WHITE) (buffer 0xFF); drawPixel clips to the widened window and indexes 'x / 8 + y * (_pw_w / 8)'; firmware drawSquare() (board_ui.cpp 80-85) paints only the one square, so the 4 extra columns stay 0xFF; nextPage() 1-page partial branch sends 'epd2.writeImage(_buffer, _pw_x, _pw_y, _pw_w, _pw_h)' and driver _writeImage re-aligns identically ('x -= x % 8; w = wb * 8') and writes the 64x60 block to RAM 0x13. Hatch check from board_ui.cpp 28-30: dots at column offsets 2,6,..58 on rows 0,4,.. and 0,4,..56 on rows 2,6,.. -> both 4-px edge strips contain dots, density 2/16 = 12.5%. dark = ((file+rank)&1)==0 so e2/e4 are light, f2/f4 dark -> stripe at x=300..303: correct. Piece disc (r+2=24 around centre 30) spans offsets 6..54 so pieces are never clipped, only hatch/border/highlight ring. Border: drawRect(0,0,480,480) only in drawFull (line 69); paintSquare line 26 fillRect wipes it on edge squares, and the 4 spill columns also wipe 4 px of top/bottom border on rank 8/1 neighbours. Status strip 480/320 are multiples of 8. Only thing I could not verify: the quoted line numbers (WebFetch gives no line numbers); irrelevant to the conclusion.

findings.claim: On this panel GxEPD2 never uses the controller's partial window for the refresh: usePartialUpdateWindow=false means command 0x91 is not sent, so EVERY 'partial' refresh is a whole-screen differential refresh with the OTP fast LUT, costing ~435 ms (author's measurement; Good Display says 0.3 s @25C) independent of window size. The window only decides how many bytes go over SPI. Consequences: (1) the firmware's three sequential refreshes per move cost ~3 x 0.44 = ~1.32-1.35 s (+~130 ms _PowerOn when the previous operation was a full refresh, because the full path ends with powerOff()), plus ~0.44 s for the selection tap = ~1.8 s blocking per tap-tap move; the on-screen 'dt' only measures the first two. (2) A single refresh costs ~0.45 s + SPI: ~0.45 s if only dirty rects are sent (~2.6 kB), ~0.55-0.7 s with display(true) sending all 48 kB at the default 4 MHz (96 ms wire time + per-byte register-polling overhead; estimate, not measured). Net gain ~0.7-0.9 s per move (2-3x). (3) There is no limit on partial window size: full-screen partial is a supported path (refresh(true) == refresh(0,0,WIDTH,HEIGHT)), used by the author's own example.
findings.evidence: Driver refresh(x,y,w,h) lines 262-266: 'if (!_using_partial_mode) _Init_Part(); if (usePartialUpdateWindow) _writeCommand(0x91); // partial in / _setPartialRamArea(x1, y1, w1, h1); _Update_Part(); if (usePartialUpdateWindow) _writeCommand(0x92);' with header 'usePartialUpdateWindow = false; // set false for better image'. _Update_Part: '_writeCommand(0x12); _waitWhileBusy("_Update_Part", partial_refresh_time);' and 'partial_refresh_time = 450; // ms, e.g. 435000us'. refresh(bool) line 238: 'if (partial_update_mode) refresh(0, 0, WIDTH, HEIGHT);'. _Init_Part: TSFIX 'E0 02' + 'E5 6E // 110' (OTP fast partial LUT), VCOM/data 0x50=0x29 'N2OCP: copy new to old' (hence writeImageAgain is an empty override). nextPage full branch ends with 'epd2.powerOff();' and _PowerOff sets '_using_partial_mode = false' -> next partial runs _Init_Part + _PowerOn ('power_on_time = 140; // ms, e.g. 129018us'). Example deepSleepTestPartialUpdate uses 'display.setPartialWindow(0, 0, display.width(), display.height());'. Core SPI: SPIClass::transfer -> spiTransferByteNL = per-byte register write + busy-poll (esp32-hal-spi.c lines 1376-1399). Good Display product page: 'Full refresh for 3s, Fast refresh for 1.5s, Partial refresh for 0.3s (tested at 25C)'. main.cpp lines 68-75: dt measured before drawStatus.
findings.recommended_action: Restructure BoardUI around ONE refresh per user-visible event. API choice: (A) simplest, pure GxEPD2_BW: call setFullWindow() once, draw with GFX straight into the persistent buffer (no firstPage, no fillScreen, no setPartialWindow - drawPixel's stride depends on _pw_w so mixing modes corrupts the buffer), then display.display(true) for a whole-screen differential refresh, or display.displayWindow(x,y,w,h) for a byte-aligned bounding box (it calls writeImagePart on the full buffer then refresh). Full refresh = display.display(false). (B) fastest: own GFXcanvas1(800,480) (same bit order/polarity: MSB first, 1=white when drawn with GxEPD_WHITE) + display.epd2.writeImagePart(canvas.getBuffer(), x,y,800,480, x,y,w,h) per dirty rect, then a single display.epd2.refresh(true); then GxEPD2_BW's own 48 kB buffer can be shrunk or the driver class used alone. Keep rects byte-aligned in x (e.g. always push the 120 px file pair) because writeImagePart rounds x down and w up independently. Use display.epd2.setBusyCallback() to poll the GT911 (and later service Lichess) during the ~0.44 s busy wait. Optionally raise SPI via the 6-arg init (SPISettings 10-20 MHz) after verifying on hardware.

verification.corrected_claim: Claim stands: with usePartialUpdateWindow=false the 0x12 refresh is never windowed (0x91/0x92 only bracket the RAM writes), so every 'partial' refresh is a whole-screen differential OTP refresh of fixed duration (~435 ms per the author's header comment; GD datasheet 0.3 s) regardless of window size; the firmware spends 3 refreshes per move + 1 per selection (~1.3 s + ~0.44 s, +~130 ms power-on after a full refresh) and dt only times two of them; full-screen partial is a supported path. Additions: (1) 435 ms assumes a current-batch panel; the header warns early batches need useFastPartialUpdateFromOTP=false, which costs ~1.58 s per partial (70-frame register LUT) - read the '_Update_Part : <us>' diagnostic line on first power-up (diag is already enabled by init(115200,...)). (2) GxEPD2_BW::_buffer is private: option A = display(true) (48 kB) or one displayWindow() bounding box per refresh; multi-rect + single refresh needs option B (own GFXcanvas1 + epd2.writeImagePart per rect + one epd2.refresh(true)). (3) GFXcanvas1 starts zero-filled = black: fillScreen(GxEPD_WHITE) before first use. (4) The 0.55-0.7 s figure for display(true) is an unmeasured estimate.
verification.reasoning: Re-read driver source. refresh(x,y,w,h): 'if (!_using_partial_mode) _Init_Part(); if (usePartialUpdateWindow) _writeCommand(0x91); // partial in / _setPartialRamArea(x1, y1, w1, h1); _Update_Part(); if (usePartialUpdateWindow) _writeCommand(0x92);' and header 'static const bool usePartialUpdateWindow = false; // set false for better image'. Note 0x91/0x92 ARE sent, but only around RAM writes in _writeImage/_writeImagePart (which end with 0x92 'partial out'), so the 0x12 refresh runs un-windowed = whole screen. Cross-check: Waveshare's epd7in5_V2.py display_Partial keeps 0x91 active through 0x12, i.e. 0x91 is what makes a refresh windowed; GxEPD2_4G README says 'on GDEY075T7 grey level partial window update looks bad (greys out remainder)'. Timing constants verbatim: 'partial_refresh_time = 450; // ms, e.g. 435000us', 'power_on_time = 140; // ms, e.g. 129018us', 'full_refresh_time = 1200; // ms, e.g. 1171000us'; _waitWhileBusy polls the real BUSY pin so these are the author's observations, not enforced delays. refresh(bool): 'if (partial_update_mode) refresh(0, 0, WIDTH, HEIGHT);'. _Init_Part: E0 02 / E5 6E; _InitDisplay 0x50 = 0x29 'N2OCP: copy new to old'; writeImageAgain is '{}' in the header. nextPage full branch ends 'epd2.powerOff();' and _PowerOff sets '_using_partial_mode = false' -> next partial re-runs _Init_Part + _PowerOn. main.cpp: refreshes at lines 56 (select), 71, 72, 75; dt taken at line 73 before drawStatus. Good Display page 396 and the T01 page 483 both: Full 3 s / Fast 1.5 s / Partial 0.3 s. GxEPD2_EPD ctor: '_spi_settings(4000000, MSBFIRST, SPI_MODE0)'; local core SPI.cpp:226-231 transfer() -> spiTransferByteNL (esp32-hal-spi.c:1376-1399: per-byte data_buf write, cmd.update spin, cmd.usr spin). 6-arg init, setBusyCallback, displayWindow(), display(bool), deepSleepTestPartialUpdate's 'setPartialWindow(0, 0, display.width(), display.height())' all verified verbatim. GFXcanvas1 bit order verified in Adafruit_GFX.cpp ('*ptr |= 0x80 >> (x & 7)' when color != 0) = same as GxEPD2_BW. Caveats found: (a) header also says 'useFastPartialUpdateFromOTP = true; // set this false for earlier batches, such as the panel I have (1580258us)' and README history says 'GDEY075T7 uses a b/w waveform written to registers, OTP version is faulty' -> on an old-batch panel the fallback register LUT is T1+T2+T3+T4 = 30+5+30+5 = 70 frames = ~1.58 s per partial; a panel bought in 2026 should be the new batch but this is unverified until hardware arrives. (b) GxEPD2_BW::_buffer is private, so option A can only push the whole 48 kB (display(true)) or ONE bounding box per refresh (displayWindow); several dirty rects + one refresh requires option B. (c) GFXcanvas1 mallocs and memset(0)s = all BLACK in GxEPD2 polarity -> fillScreen(GxEPD_WHITE) first. (d) SPI per-byte overhead on S3 is unmeasured; 48 kB could cost 0.2-0.4 s rather than ~0.1-0.25 s, which favours dirty rects over display(true).

findings.claim: The firmware leaves the panel's high-voltage supply switched on indefinitely: GxEPD2 only calls powerOff() after FULL refreshes; after any partial refresh power stays on until the application calls powerOff()/hibernate(), which the firmware never does. In a chess game that means the booster runs for minutes while the player thinks (battery drain, and the library author notes powerOff 'avoids screen fading over time'). Costs: powerOff() ~40 ms now, then +~130 ms (_InitDisplay + _PowerOn) on the next refresh, controller RAM is kept (the library's own flow relies on this after every full refresh). hibernate() additionally puts the UC8179 in deep sleep (0x07,0xA5); wake needs a HW reset and the controller's previous-image buffer must be restored with firstPage()/nextPageToPrevious() followed by a full-screen partial window, i.e. 2 x 48 kB SPI writes + reset + power-on = roughly +0.4-0.8 s on the first move after hibernate (estimate).
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_BW.h nextPage partial branch (lines 433-442) has no powerOff; full branch line 452 'epd2.powerOff();'; display(): 'if (!partial_update_mode) epd2.powerOff();'. Header comments lines 768/773: 'turns off generation of panel driving voltages, avoids screen fading over time' / 'turns powerOff() and sets controller to deep sleep for minimum power use, ONLY if wakeable by RST'. Driver hibernate(): '_PowerOff(); ... _writeCommand(0x07); // deep sleep / _writeData(0xA5);' and _InitDisplay: 'if (_hibernating) _reset();'. Example deepSleepTestPartialUpdate: 'display.hibernate(); delay(10000); // Restore previous buffer // so far only implemented for GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 ... while (display.nextPageToPrevious()); ... display.setPartialWindow(0, 0, display.width(), display.height());'. grep of firmware main.cpp/board_ui.cpp: no powerOff/hibernate calls. Good Display: 'Standby Power: 0.0165 mW', refresh 26.4 mW.
findings.recommended_action: Call display.powerOff() after each move's single refresh, or after ~2-3 s of touch inactivity so that a quick select->move pair does not pay 130 ms twice. Reserve display.hibernate() for just before ESP32 deep sleep; on wake either do a fast full refresh (simplest, one 1.2 s flash) or restore with nextPageToPrevious() + full-screen partial for a flash-free wake. The standby-vs-deep-sleep saving is microamps and irrelevant next to the ESP32-S3.

verification.corrected_claim: Claim stands: GxEPD2 powers the panel off only after full refreshes; after any partial refresh the booster stays on until the application calls powerOff()/hibernate(), and the firmware never does. Cost of fixing: ~40 ms powerOff + ~130 ms (_InitDisplay + _PowerOn) on the next refresh, controller RAM retained (same flow the library uses after every full refresh). hibernate() = POF + deep sleep 0x07/0xA5, woken by HW reset inside _InitDisplay; previous-image RAM must then be restored (nextPageToPrevious, requires GxEPD2 >= 1.6.8 -> bump lib_deps) or a full refresh done. Correction of emphasis: the main reason is panel stress/fading (Waveshare: prolonged high-voltage state damages the panel irreparably), the battery saving is unquantified and at most ~8 mA. Because the Seeed board keeps the panel powered during ESP32 deep sleep, re-init after wake with display.init(115200, false, 2, false) allows immediate partial refresh if the controller was only powered off, not hibernated.
verification.reasoning: Verified in source: GxEPD2_BW::nextPage() partial branch (1 page) = writeImage + refresh + writeImageAgain, no powerOff; full branch ends 'epd2.powerOff();'; display(): 'if (!partial_update_mode) epd2.powerOff();'. README history: 'fixed (added) powerOff() after full update (partial update keeps power on)'. Header comments verbatim: 'turns off generation of panel driving voltages, avoids screen fading over time' / 'turns powerOff() and sets controller to deep sleep for minimum power use, ONLY if wakeable by RST (rst >= 0)'. Driver: _PowerOff sends 0x02 and clears _power_is_on and _using_partial_mode; hibernate() = _PowerOff + 0x07/0xA5 + _hibernating=true; _InitDisplay: 'if (_hibernating) _reset();'. Constants 'power_off_time = 42; // ms, e.g. 40430us', 'power_on_time = 140; // ms, e.g. 129018us'. grep of firmware src/ for powerOff|hibernate: zero hits. The author's own example calls display.powerOff() three times in setup() after partial-update demos, and deepSleepTestPartialUpdate does hibernate -> firstPage/nextPageToPrevious -> setPartialWindow(0,0,width,height), comment '// Restore previous buffer // so far only implemented for GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7'. Good Display page: 'Standby Power Consumption: 0.0165 mW', 'Power Consumption of the Refresh: 26.4 mW'. RAM retention across POF is an inference, but a safe one: the library itself does full refresh -> powerOff -> differential partial on every first move. Two things the researcher missed: (1) the stronger argument is panel health, not battery - Waveshare's precautions for the sister 7.5" V2 panel (whose driver uses the identical E0 02 / E5 5A / E5 6E sequences) say the screen must be put to sleep or powered off when not refreshing, otherwise it 'will remain in a high voltage state for a long time, which will damage the e-Paper and cannot be repaired'. The idle-with-booster-on current is not published, upper bound is the 26.4 mW refresh figure (~8 mA), small next to an awake ESP32-S3, so the battery argument alone would be minor. (2) writeImageToPrevious/nextPageToPrevious exist only since 1.6.8 (README: 'Version 1.6.8 - added methods writeImageToPrevious and writeImagePartToPrevious to b/w driver classes'); lib_deps '^1.6.2' happens to resolve to 1.6.9 today but should be raised to ^1.6.8 if the flash-free wake is used. Discussion #126 is about init(..., initial=false) after MCU deep sleep ('initial false for re-init after processor deep sleep wake up, if display power supply was kept'), relevant here because the Seeed board has no load switch so the panel supply IS kept during ESP32 deep sleep.

findings.claim: Ghosting policy in the firmware is ~16x laxer than the manufacturer's recommendation and its 'full refresh' is not a true full refresh. partialCount is incremented once per MOVE, but a move performs 4 partial refreshes (select, from, to, status), so ~80 partial refreshes happen between drawFull() calls; Good Display recommends a full-screen refresh after every 5 consecutive fast/partial operations. Moreover GxEPD2's full refresh for this panel is the OTP 'fast full' (forced temperature 0x5A, ~1.17 s, one flash), which Good Display itself classes as 'Fast Refresh'; the true multi-flash ~3 s full refresh requires useFastFullUpdate=false, a compile-time static const in the library header (not switchable at run time, _Update_Full is private). Fast waveforms are selected by faking the temperature (TSFIX), and the author says to disable fast full for the 'extended (low) temperature range'; panel operating range is 0-50 C.
findings.evidence: main.cpp line 80: 'if (++partialCount % 20 == 0) ui.drawFull(board, status);' executed once per completed move; lines 56, 71, 72, 75 are the four partial refreshes. Good Display page: 'When using Fast Refresh and Partial Refresh, it is recommended to perform a Full-Screen Refresh after every five consecutive operations.' / 'Fast Refresh: The screen flickers once' / 'Operating temperature: 0-50 C'. Driver _Update_Full: 'if (useFastFullUpdate) { E0 02 // TSFIX; E5 5A // 90 } else { E0 00; 41 00 // internal temperature sensor }'; header 'useFastFullUpdate = true; // set false for extended (low) temperature range', 'full_refresh_time = 1200; // ms, e.g. 1171000us'. Example showBox: '// avoid ghosting caused by OTP waveform / display.clearScreen(); display.refresh(false);' for GDEW075T7/GDEY075T7. GxEPD2_4G README: 'ghosting can't be avoided; using clearScreen() helps'.
findings.recommended_action: Count refreshes, not moves, and make the threshold a config constant; start at one fast-full every ~8-10 partial refreshes and tune by eye (after merging to one refresh per move that is every ~5 moves), scheduled at natural pauses (while the engine thinks / when the opponent's Lichess move arrives). Do a true slow full refresh at game start/end: the clean way is to vendor the two driver files into the project under a new class name (GPL-3.0, template accepts any GxEPD2_EPD subclass) and turn useFastFullUpdate into a run-time flag. Indoor use only needs the defaults.

verification.corrected_claim: Claim stands: the counter ticks once per move while each move costs 4 partial refreshes (more with deselects), so ~80+ partials run between full refreshes vs Good Display's 'every five consecutive operations' (16x); and GxEPD2's 'full' refresh on this panel is the single-flash OTP fast mode (TSFIX, forced temp 0x5A, ~1.17 s), the same sequence Waveshare calls init_fast; the true multi-flash ~3 s refresh needs useFastFullUpdate=false, a compile-time static const. Corrections: the 'avoid ghosting caused by OTP waveform' code lives in drawBitmaps800x480(), not showBox(); and a run-time slow full refresh does not require vendoring the driver - a small subclass using the protected _writeCommand/_writeData/_waitWhileBusy/_using_partial_mode members is enough (must reset _using_partial_mode=false afterwards). The 8-10 threshold is a tuning suggestion, not sourced.
verification.reasoning: main.cpp re-read: line 80 'if (++partialCount % 20 == 0) ui.drawFull(board, status);' is reached only on a completed move (select path returns at line 58, deselect at 64), while partial refreshes occur at lines 56, 71, 72, 75 (+62 on deselect) -> >= 80 partial refreshes between full refreshes although the comment says 'Ogni 20 partial refresh'. Good Display page 396 verbatim: 'When using Fast Refresh and Partial Refresh, it is recommended to perform a Full-Screen Refresh after every five consecutive operations.' and 'Full Refresh: ... the screen may flicker multiple times. Fast Refresh: The screen flickers once ... Partial Refresh: The screen does not flicker'; 'Operating Temperature: 0-50 C'; refresh times 3 / 1.5 / 0.3 s (same on the T01 page 483). 80/5 = 16x: arithmetic correct. Driver _Update_Full verbatim: 'if (useFastFullUpdate) { E0 02 // TSFIX; E5 5A // 90 } else { E0 00 ...; 41 00 // TSE ... }' and header 'static const bool useFastFullUpdate = true; // set false for extended (low) temperature range', 'full_refresh_time = 1200; // ms, e.g. 1171000us'. Independent corroboration that 0x5A IS the manufacturer's 'fast' mode: Waveshare epd7in5_V2.py init_fast() sends E0 02 / E5 5A, init_part() sends E0 02 / E5 6E. _Update_Full/_Init_Full are private and the flag is static const -> not switchable through the stock API. Two corrections: (1) the '// avoid ghosting caused by OTP waveform / display.clearScreen(); display.refresh(false);' snippet is in drawBitmaps800x480(), not showBox() (showBox has no such code) - evidence misattributed, conclusion unaffected. (2) Vendoring is not the only route: GxEPD2_EPD declares _writeCommand, _writeData, _waitWhileBusy, _power_is_on, _using_partial_mode as protected and refresh() as virtual, so a ~15-line subclass of GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7 (GxEPD2_BW<MyEpd, MyEpd::HEIGHT>) can add a slowFullRefresh() that sends E0 00 / 41 00 / 12, waits busy, then sets _using_partial_mode=false (mandatory, otherwise the next partial keeps TSFIX off and runs the slow waveform) and powers off. GxEPD2_4G README quote 'ghosting can't be avoided; using clearScreen() helps' verified. GD's 5-refresh figure is conservative (author's own demo does far more partials in a row), so the researcher's 8-10 starting point is a judgement call, not a sourced number.

findings.claim: 4-grey is NOT available in GxEPD2 for this panel. It exists only in the separate library GxEPD2_4G (>= 1.0.8 supports GDEY075T7), where grey-level partial window update 'looks bad (greys out remainder)' and is disabled by default; grey refreshes are flashing full-type refreshes, so they cannot be used for per-move updates. Dithered/hatched 1-bit patterns are the right choice for dark squares, and need GxEPD2 >= 1.5.9, which added the PWS register write specifically because of an issue with dithered bitmaps on GDEY075T7.
findings.evidence: GxEPD2_4G README: 'Version 1.0.8 - added support for GDEY075T7 800x480 - on GDEY075T7 grey level partial window update looks bad (greys out remainder) - on GDEY075T7 grey level partial window update is disabled by default'; '4 grey level support can be used instead of differential refresh'; 'ghosting can't be avoided'. GxEPD2 README 1.5.9: 'added Power Save command (PWS) to GDEY075T7 init (issue with dithered bitmaps)'; driver _InitDisplay: '_writeCommand(0xE3); // PWS / _writeData(0x22); // VCOM 2 line period, Source 2 * 660ns'. Good Display lists the panel as '4 grayscale levels'.
findings.recommended_action: Stay 1-bit. On first hardware test compare 3-4 dark-square textures side by side after 10 partial refreshes (current 12.5% dots, 25% ordered dither, 45-degree line hatch, 50% checker) and pick by legibility and ghosting; the current 12.5% may read as too faint behind the touch glass.

findings.claim: Calling SPI.begin(sck, miso, mosi, ss) BEFORE display.init() is the correct, author-documented way to remap pins on ESP32; GxEPD2's internal _pSPIx->begin() then becomes a no-op. selectSPI()/the 6-argument init() only choose the SPIClass instance and SPISettings, they cannot set pins. On the XIAO ESP32-S3 (Plus) variant the defaults are already SCK=7, MISO=8, MOSI=9, so the call is redundant but harmless. One wart: the firmware passes EPD_MISO=8, which is also BUZZER_PIN; SPI attaches GPIO8 as MISO and the first tone() re-assigns it to LEDC. On the installed core 3.3.8 this happens to be safe (detaching MISO alone does not stop the bus), but it depends on peripheral-manager internals.
findings.evidence: Core SPI.cpp lines 66-69: 'bool SPIClass::begin(int8_t sck, int8_t miso, int8_t mosi, int8_t ss) { if (_spi) { return true; }'; line 121: 'if (_miso >= 0 && !spiAttachMISO(_spi, _miso))' (so -1 is accepted; only all-four -1 selects defaults). GxEPD2_EPD.cpp line 66: '_pSPIx->begin(); // may steal _rst pin'; selectSPI lines 105-109 only stores pointer+settings. GxEPD2_Example.ino lines 193-194: '// SPI.begin(sck, miso, mosi, ss); // preset for remapped pins / SPI.begin(18, -1, 16, 33); // my LOLIN ESP32 S2 mini connection'. variants/XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus/pins_arduino.h: 'SS = 44; MOSI = 9; MISO = 8; SCK = 7'. esp32-hal-spi.c spiDetachBus lines 217-231: bus is stopped only when 'spi->sck == -1 || (spi->miso == -1 && spi->mosi == -1)'; esp32-hal-periman.c perimanSetPinBus lines 145-153 calls the previous bus type's deinit when a pin changes owner. Firmware main.cpp lines 29-30 and config.h lines 14, 24.
findings.recommended_action: Use SPI.begin(EPD_SCK, -1, EPD_MOSI, -1); display.init(...). The display is write-only, so MISO is never needed and GPIO8 stays exclusively the buzzer's; SS=-1 is fine because GxEPD2 toggles CS by digitalWrite. Remove EPD_MISO from config.h.

findings.claim: Piece rendering on 1-bit e-paper at 60 px: use two 1-bit bitmaps per piece - a MASK (filled silhouette dilated ~2 px) drawn in white, then the INK drawn in black. This gives white pieces an opaque white interior and every piece a white halo, so a solid black piece stays legible on a hatched dark square. Fonts are the wrong tool (single colour, no mask, and chess TTFs are mostly 'freeware'/non-commercial). GPL-3.0-compatible sets according to lichess COPYING.md: cburnett, mono, merida (GPLv2+), mpchess (GPLv3+, designed for printed b/w diagrams), fantasy/spatial/celtic (MIT), chessnut (Apache-2.0), rhosgfx (CC0), kiwen-suwi/Firi/totoy/papercut (CC BY 4.0, attribution needed), shapes (CC BY-SA 4.0, one-way compatible with GPLv3). NOT usable for a MakerWorld release: every CC BY-NC-SA set (staunty, maestro, fresca, cardinal, gioco, tatiana, california, horsey, ...), alpha ('free for personal non commercial use'), chess7/companion/leipzig ('freeware').
findings.evidence: lila COPYING.md rows: 'public/piece/cburnett | Colin M.L. Burnett | GPLv2+', 'public/piece/mono | Thibault Duplessis and Colin M.L. Burnett | GPLv2+', 'public/piece/merida | Armando Hernandez Marroquin | GPLv2+', 'public/piece/mpchess | Maxime Chupin | GPL3v3+', 'public/piece/fantasy|spatial|celtic | Maurizio Monge | MIT', 'public/piece/chessnut | Alexis Luengas | Apache 2.0', 'public/piece/rhosgfx | RhosGFX | CC0 1.0', 'public/piece/staunty | sadsnake1 | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0', 'public/piece/alpha | Eric Bentzen | "free for personal non commercial use"'. GxEPD2_BW derives from Adafruit_GFX, so drawBitmap(x,y,bitmap,w,h,color) (MSB-first, transparent background) and drawXBitmap (LSB-first XBM) are available; GxEPD2_BW.h also offers drawInvertedBitmap. Size: 12 pieces x 2 bitmaps x (8 bytes x 60 rows) = 11.5 kB flash. cburnett SVGs use a 45x45 viewBox with 1.5-unit strokes = 2 px at 60 px, which survives thresholding (inference from the SVG geometry, not tested). FSF/CC compatibility statements (CC BY 4.0 compatible with all GPL versions; CC BY-SA 4.0 one-way to GPLv3) taken from search-result summaries of gnu.org/fsf.org, the gnu.org page itself returned HTTP 429.
findings.recommended_action: Ship an offline converter in the repo (Python: rasterise SVG at 52-56 px without antialiasing -> threshold -> ink array; fill + dilate 2 px -> mask array; emit a PROGMEM header) together with the source SVGs, so the 'preferred form for modification' is in the GPL repo and makers can swap sets. Start with cburnett (most recognisable, GPLv2+) and try mpchess as the print-style alternative. Draw order per square: background texture -> mask in GxEPD_WHITE -> ink in GxEPD_BLACK -> highlight frame last. Hand-retouch knight and queen after thresholding.

findings.claim: Side finding from the Seeed schematic (outside the GxEPD2 thread but it affects the roadmap): the driver board has no battery-voltage divider to any XIAO pin, the e-paper 3V3 rail is simply the XIAO's 3V3 pin through a ferrite bead with a 220 uF bulk capacitor (no separate regulator, no load switch), and all of D0-D10 are consumed by the planned pin map. So the phase-4 'battery gauge' cannot be implemented with the BOM as ordered; it needs a 2-resistor divider from BAT to a free ADC1 pin, and on the XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus the only free ADC1-capable pad is GPIO10 (D16, bottom/castellated pad). GxEPD2's README warns that 7.5" panels are unreliable when fed from a weak 3.3 V pin; Seeed validates this exact combination and adds the 220 uF, so it should be fine, but brown-outs during WiFi + refresh are the first thing to suspect if the image fades or the ESP32 resets.
findings.evidence: Schematic 'ePAPER' Rev 1.0, seeedstudio, 2024-12-09: U1 ETA9740E8A with R5 360K ('Charging current = 0.5A'), BAT -> power switch CN_MSK12CO2 -> BAT_4V2, OUT -> VDD_5V -> XIAO 5V pin; FB1 HCB1608KF-181T20 from 3V3 to the display rail with CT1 220uF/10V; booster Q1 Si1304BDL, L1 10uH, D1/D2/D5 B0540WS, R2 0R47; header nets A0_D0_RST, A1_D1_CS, A2_D2_BUSY, A3_D3_DC, A4_D4_SDA, A5_D5_SCL, A6_D6_TX, A7_D7_RX, A8_D8_SCK, A9_D9_MISO, A10_D10_MOSI; no net from BAT_4V2 to any GPIO. Botland lists 'ePaper Driver Board for Seeed Xiao V2 - Seeedstudio 114993558', matching the wiki page. GxEPD2 README: 'note that 7.5" e-paper displays don't work reliable if fed from 3.3V Arduino pin'. Plus variant pins_arduino.h: 'D16 = 10'.
findings.recommended_action: Decide now (before the case is designed) whether a battery gauge matters: if yes, plan a 2x ~470k divider + 100 nF from the battery JST to GPIO10/D16 on the XIAO Plus underside, and leave room/wire routing for it in the 3D-printed case. Let the hardware thread double-check ETA9740 light-load behaviour before relying on deep sleep.

verification.corrected_claim: Claim stands: the Seeed driver board (SKU 114993558, schematic 'ePAPER' Rev 1.0) has no battery divider to any XIAO pin, the panel rail is the XIAO 3V3 pin via ferrite bead FB1 + 220 uF (no regulator/load switch), and D0-D10 are all used, so a battery gauge needs an external 2-resistor divider into an ADC1 pin; under the current pin map the only free one is GPIO10 (D16 on the Plus, a half-hole/bottom pad). Clarifications: the Plus variant's 'ADC_BAT = 10 / BAT_VOLT_PIN' define and the wiki's 'Read the BAT voltage value' are labels only - Seeed's Plus V1.1 schematic has no divider on that net, and it would sense the wrong battery node anyway. The driver board exposes BAT_4V2/GND on DNP pads H1/H2 (battery side of the power switch) as the tap point. Alternative without bottom-pad soldering: poll the GT911 without INT, buzzer -> D6/GPIO43, divider -> D9/GPIO8. With board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3 in platformio.ini, address the pin as raw GPIO 10. Seeed's schematic note sizes the charger for a 1000 mAh cell at 0.5 A (4000 mAh -> ~9-10 h charge). ETA9740 light-load behaviour remains unverified.
verification.reasoning: I opened the Seeed schematic PDF myself (title 'ePAPER', OrgName seeedstudio, Designer Gongjun, Rev 1.0, Monday, December 09, 2024). Seen: U1 ETA9740E8A, OUT(7) -> VDD_5V -> XIAO 5V pin, ISET R5 360K_1%, note 'Charging current = 0.5A' and 'BAT: 4.2V 1000mAH', L2 1uH; CN5 CN_BAT -> BAT_4V2 (C24 22uF); power switch CN6 CN_MSK12CO2-SZ between BAT_4V2 and U1 BAT(6); FB1 HCB1608KF-181T20 from 3V3 with C2 104, C3 105, CT1 220uF/10V feeding L1 10uH / Q1 Si1304BDL / R2 0R47 / D1,D2,D5 B0540WS booster; CN_DISPLAY carries only A2_D2_BUSY, A0_D0_RST, A3_D3_DC, A1_D1_CS, A8_D8_SCK, A10_D10_MOSI + 3V3; A9_D9_MISO, A4/A5 (SDA/SCL), A6/A7 (TX/RX) go to headers only (so buzzer on D9 and touch on D4-D7 do not collide with the board). BAT_4V2 touches only CN5, CN6, C24 and two DNP pads H1 (BAT_4V2) / H2 (GND): no divider, no GPIO. No regulator or load switch on the display rail. Seeed product page p-6374 shows SKU 114993558 and the V2 wiki links exactly this PDF; wiki lists 7.5" mono 800x480 as supported and mentions no battery ADC. GxEPD2 README quote verified verbatim. Tried to refute 'no gauge possible' via the XIAO Plus: its variant pins_arduino.h has 'static const uint8_t ADC_BAT = 10; #define BAT_VOLT_PIN ADC_BAT' and 'D16 = 10', and the Seeed wiki pin table says 'ADC_BAT | GPIO10 | Read the BAT voltage value' - which suggests an on-board divider. But the XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus V1.1 schematic (KiCad, 2026-01-15) shows net IO10/XMCLK/ADC_BAT going only to ESP32-S3 GPIO10, half-hole pad 20 of U2 'XIAO-HALF-HOLE-23P' and B2B J3; the battery section is just SGM40567 charger + PMOS + SGM6029 buck, no divider. Seeed forum thread confirms (users: 'I don't see any evidence that this pin is actually connected to the battery circuit'; workaround 2x200k + 100nF). And even a divider on the XIAO would sense the XIAO's own BAT pad, which is unused here because the cell sits behind the ETA9740 on the driver board. ADC1 on ESP32-S3 = GPIO1-10; GPIO1-9 = D0-D5, D8-D10 are all taken by the plan, D6/D7 = GPIO43/44 are not ADC, D17-D19 = GPIO13/12/11 are ADC2 (conflicts with Wi-Fi) -> GPIO10 is indeed the only free ADC1 pad under the current pin map. Additions: H1/H2 give a ready solder point but sit on the battery side of the switch (always live; ~4.5 uA through 2x470k, plus uA-level back-feed through the GPIO clamp when the XIAO is off - harmless, but tapping after the switch at C17/C18 avoids it). The pin map is still changeable, so a no-bottom-pad alternative exists: run the GT911 polled (no INT), move the buzzer to D6/GPIO43 and put the divider on D9/GPIO8 (ADC1_CH7). platformio.ini uses board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3 (non-Plus variant) where D16/ADC_BAT are undefined - use raw GPIO 10. 0.5 A charge current means ~9-10 h for the 4000 mAh cell. Not verified: ETA9740 light-load/auto-shutdown behaviour (no datasheet fetched).

findings.claim: platformio.ini is not reproducible for other makers and targets the wrong board ID. 'platform = espressif32' only yields Arduino core 3.3.8 on Fabrizio's machine because pioarduino 55.03.38 is installed under that name; anyone else gets the official PlatformIO platform (Arduino core 2.0.x), where the SPI/LEDC/peripheral-manager behaviour analysed above differs. 'board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3' is the 8 MB non-Plus definition combined with default_16MB.csv; it flashes only because upload uses '--flash-size detect'. A dedicated seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus board (16 MB, qio_opi, variant XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus) exists in the installed platform.
findings.evidence: ~/.platformio/platforms/espressif32/platform.json: 'repository.url: https://github.com/pioarduino/platform-espressif32.git', 'version: 55.03.38', framework 'esp32-core-3.3.8'; .piopm uri 'https://github.com/pioarduino/platform-espressif32/releases/download/55.03.38-1/platform-espressif32.zip'. boards/seeed_xiao_esp32s3.json: 'flash_size: 8MB', 'maximum_size: 8388608'; boards/seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus.json: 'flash_size: 16MB', 'variant: XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus', 'memory_type: qio_opi' (its default partitions is default_8MB.csv). default_16MB.csv: app1 at 0x650000 size 0x640000 (beyond 8 MB). builder/main.py upload flags: '--flash-size', 'detect'. Firmware platformio.ini lines 4-10.
findings.recommended_action: For the release pin the platform by URL (platform = https://github.com/pioarduino/platform-espressif32/releases/download/55.03.38-1/platform-espressif32.zip), set board = seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus, keep board_build.partitions = default_16MB.csv, drop the now-duplicate BOARD_HAS_PSRAM / ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT flags, and pin GxEPD2 and Adafruit GFX to exact versions.

unknowns: Real partial-refresh time of Fabrizio's panel batch: the author measured 435 ms with the OTP fast-partial LUT but notes 'set this false for earlier batches, such as the panel I have (1580258us)'; Good Display quotes 0.3 s. The -T01 touch variant could be from a different batch. Must be read from GxEPD2's diag output ('_Update_Part : <us>') on first power-up; if it is ~1.5 s, useFastPartialUpdateFromOTP has to be flipped (library patch) and all timing estimates change.

SPI cost of writing the full 48 kB frame on ESP32-S3 with GxEPD2's per-byte transfer(): my 0.1-0.25 s at 4 MHz is an estimate from reading spiTransferByteNL, not a measurement. Maximum SPI clock the UC8179 accepts was not verified (datasheet not read).

Whether the UC8179 formally guarantees RAM retention in standby after power-off (0x02): inferred from the fact that GxEPD2 calls powerOff() after every full refresh and then performs window-only partial writes; not confirmed from the datasheet.

UC8179 minimum RST low pulse width (so whether reset_duration=2 is strictly in spec) - not verified; Good Display's GDEY075T7-T01 ESP32 sample code (https://www.good-display.com/companyfile/1838.html) was not downloaded.
The exact nature of the 'issue with dithered bitmaps' fixed by PWS in GxEPD2 1.5.9 - the originating discussion was not located, so I cannot say which dither densities were affected.
No numeric low-temperature threshold is given anywhere for when fast-full/fast-partial waveforms stop working well; only 'set false for extended (low) temperature range' and the 0-50 C panel rating.
Idle current of the panel with the HV booster left on (no powerOff) - not found in any source; only 26.4 mW refresh and 0.0165 mW standby are published.
How visible 12.5% hatch, the 4-px stripes and partial-refresh ghosts are through the laminated capacitive touch glass - needs the hardware.
ETA9740 (power-bank IC) light-load / no-load auto-shutdown behaviour, which could cut the 5 V rail when the ESP32 deep-sleeps - datasheet not read; belongs to the hardware thread.
gnu.org licence list returned HTTP 429; CC BY 4.0 / CC BY-SA 4.0 GPL-compatibility statements come from search-result summaries and the FSF blog title, not from a verbatim read of the page.
Whether cburnett/mpchess SVGs threshold cleanly at 52-60 px (stroke survival on knight/queen) - reasoned from SVG geometry, not rendered.
questions_for_user: When the panel arrives: what is printed on the display's FPC tail (e.g. 'FPC-C001 xx.xx.xx') and what does the serial log show for '_Update_Part' and '_Update_Full' (microseconds) on the first run? This decides whether the OTP fast-partial setting is right for your batch.

How much flashing do you accept? Options: a 1.2 s single black flash every ~5 moves (scheduled while the engine/opponent is thinking), plus a 3 s multi-flash deep clean only at game start/end - or do you prefer fewer flashes and tolerate some ghosting like the Atlas does?

Are you OK with vendoring a patched copy of the GxEPD2 GDEY075T7 driver class inside the firmware repo (GPL-3.0, needed for a run-time switch between fast-full and true full refresh and possibly the OTP flag), or must the project build against the unmodified upstream library only?

Tap feedback: should selecting a piece cost an e-ink refresh (~0.45 s: highlight frame and, in phase 2, legal-move dots), or do you prefer instant buzzer-only feedback on the first tap and a single refresh when the move is completed?

Piece style: classic Wikipedia/lichess 'cburnett', 'merida', or the print-diagram look of 'mpchess'? Are you fine with GPL artwork + an attribution/credits screen, and with the firmware being GPL-3.0-or-later (required anyway by GxEPD2 and the CT-800 engine)?

Dark squares: light dot hatch as now (12.5%), a denser 25% dither, or diagonal line hatching like printed chess books? And do you want a-h / 1-8 coordinates on the board edge (that would favour 56 px byte-aligned squares, 448 px board, instead of 60 px)?

Do you want a battery percentage on screen? The Seeed driver board has no battery sense line, so it needs two resistors soldered to a bottom pad (GPIO10/D16) of the XIAO Plus and space for that in the case - better decided before you model the enclosure.
Will the board ever be used in the cold (below ~10-15 C, e.g. outdoors/terrace)? If yes the fast waveforms should be made switchable to the slow temperature-compensated ones.
